es: Elaborar un mini informe sobre el transporte escolar y presentarlo en un resumen oral de un minuto con punto clave, cautela y recomendación.

teaching.en: In brief, this report gives an overview of how students make their daily commute to school, according to a survey of one hundred families.
teaching.es: En resumen, este informe ofrece una visión general de cómo hacen los estudiantes su trayecto diario al colegio, según una encuesta a cien familias.
teaching.explanationEs: In brief resume en una frase; give an overview introduce el panorama general; commute es el trayecto diario al colegio o al trabajo.
segments: In brief, this report gives an overview of how students make their
daily commute to school, according to a survey of one hundred families.
teaching.audioText: In brief, this report gives an overview of how students make their daily commute to school, according to a survey of one hundred families.

teaching.en: I will outline the main findings in one minute, so I will pick out only the two or three figures that matter most to the listeners.
teaching.es: Presentaré a grandes rasgos los principales resultados en un minuto, así que seleccionaré solo las dos o tres cifras que más importan a los oyentes.
teaching.explanationEs: I will outline… es la fórmula oral para anunciar el resumen; pick out es elegir lo más importante y dejar lo demás.
segments: I will outline the main findings in one minute, so I will pick
out only the two or three figures that matter most to the listeners.
teaching.audioText: I will outline the main findings in one minute, so I will pick out only the two or three figures that matter most to the listeners.

teaching.en: The key point is that most students depend on the school bus, and that is the key takeaway I want the audience to remember.
teaching.es: La idea clave es que la mayoría de los estudiantes depende del autobús escolar, y esa es la idea principal que quiero que recuerde el público.
teaching.explanationEs: The key point is that… da la idea central; en una presentación oral se dice una sola vez y se repite al final como key takeaway.
segments: The key point is that most students depend on the school bus,
and that is the key takeaway I want the audience to remember.
teaching.audioText: The key point is that most students depend on the school bus, and that is the key takeaway I want the audience to remember.

teaching.en: To conclude, it appears that late buses are the main problem, although more evidence is needed before we can be certain.
teaching.es: Para concluir, parece que los autobuses con retraso son el problema principal, aunque hacen falta más pruebas antes de poder estar seguros.
teaching.explanationEs: To conclude cierra el resumen; se mantiene la cautela de las clases anteriores (it appears, more evidence is needed).
segments: To conclude, it appears that late buses are the main problem,
although more evidence is needed before we can be certain.
teaching.audioText: To conclude, it appears that late buses are the main problem, although more evidence is needed before we can be certain.

teaching.en: We recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the journey for the students who live furthest from the school.
teaching.es: Recomendamos un segundo autobús por la mañana, que acortaría el trayecto de los estudiantes que viven más lejos del colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: We recommend + sustantivo o -ing; el condicional would dice el efecto esperado.
segments: We recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the
journey for the students who live furthest from the school.
teaching.audioText: We recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the journey for the students who live furthest from the school.

teaching.en: To keep the summary concise, I will mention only two findings and try to distil the report into one clear message, and I must keep to time.
teaching.es: Para que el resumen sea conciso, mencionaré solo dos resultados e intentaré condensar el informe en un mensaje claro, y debo ajustarme al tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Un resumen oral breve elige los dos o tres datos más importantes; distil es condensar, y keep to time, no pasarse del tiempo.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que abre el informe con una visión general del tema.

choices.text: This report gives a long list of every answer that each student gave in the survey.
This report gives an overview of how students travel to school, based on a survey of 100 students.
This report gives my own feelings about travelling to school with my friends every day.

feedback.es: Give an overview presenta el panorama general del tema y la base de datos; las otras opciones son una lista exhaustiva o una opinión personal.

hint.es: Busca la frase que da el panorama general y cita la base de datos, sin opiniones ni listas.

origin.text: You surveyed 100 students about how they travel to school. Fifty-two come by school bus and thirty walk. Your report needs an opening sentence that gives the reader the overall picture, before any detail.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para que el resumen sea conciso, mencionaré solo dos resultados.»

feedback.es: Concise describe un resumen breve y directo: solo lo esencial, sin repetir todo el informe.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que describe un texto breve que dice mucho con pocas palabras.

origin.text: I have only one minute for the whole talk. To keep the summary ___, I will mention only two findings and leave the rest for the written report.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Recomendamos un segundo autobús por la mañana para los que viven lejos.»

answer.text: We recommend a second morning bus for students who live far away

feedback.es: We recommend + sustantivo dice qué propones; for students who live far away precisa a quién beneficia.

hint.es: Empieza por la fórmula que introduce la recomendación.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué idea cierra el resumen la oradora.

choices.text: With a warning that the evidence is too weak to justify any action.
With a summary of the two figures she has mentioned.
With a proposal that follows from the problem she found.

feedback.es: La oradora cierra con To conclude, we recommend…: una propuesta que se deriva del problema principal.

origin.audio: Good morning. I will outline the main findings of our survey on school transport in one minute. The key point is that more than half of the students depend on the school bus. It appears that late buses are the main problem, although we need more evidence. To conclude, we recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the trip for students who live far away.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del resumen oral con su función.

pairs: I will outline the main findings.
The key point is that most use the bus.
It appears that late buses are the problem.
To conclude, we recommend a second bus.

feedback.es: Un buen resumen oral anuncia, da la idea central, matiza y cierra con una recomendación.

prompt.es: Elige la primera frase adecuada para un resumen oral de un minuto.

choices.text: I will outline our main findings in one minute.
This report, which is based on a survey carried out among students of several year groups, will now be described in full detail.
Well, there is quite a lot of stuff that we could talk about, really.

feedback.es: En un resumen oral la primera frase es corta y anuncia el plan; la opción larga es de estilo escrito y la vaga no anuncia nada.

origin.text: Here are three options for the first sentence of a one-minute talk. You have very little time, so the opening sentence must be short, clear and useful.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué debe hacer el estudiante para mejorar su resumen.

choices.text: Add more figures so that the audience trusts the results.
Keep fewer figures and sound more careful about the cause.
Move the recommendation to the start of the summary.

feedback.es: La profesora pide elegir dos cifras y sustituir la certeza sobre la causa por it appears that…

origin.audio: Your summary was clear, but it ran for almost two minutes, so you must cut it. You announced the topic well, and your key point about the school bus was memorable. However, you read out five different figures, and the audience will remember only one or two of them. Choose the two that matter most. You also sounded certain that late buses are the cause; say instead that it appears they may be the main problem. Finish with your recommendation, as you did, because it is the part that people act on.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige qué valora positivamente la profesora.

choices.text: The large number of figures that were included in it.
The certain tone used to describe the main cause.
The announcement of the topic and the final recommendation.

feedback.es: La profesora alaba el anuncio claro del tema y el cierre con la recomendación, que es lo que el público puede aplicar.

prompt.es: Completa: «En el próximo minuto presentaré brevemente los principales resultados.»

feedback.es: I will outline… es la fórmula habitual para anunciar un resumen breve de los resultados.

origin.text: Thank you all for coming. In the next minute I will briefly ___ the main findings of our survey on the commute, starting with the key point.

prompt.es: Escribe el mini informe: objetivo, método, resultados, matiz, conclusión y recomendación.

answer.text: The aim of this report is to describe how students travel to school. The method was a survey of 100 students carried out by the school council, and every answer was included in the analysis. The main findings show that 52 percent of respondents come by school bus, whereas only 6 percent cycle. The remaining students either walk, 30 percent, or come by car, 12 percent. Furthermore, 35 students said that the bus journey takes more than forty minutes. It appears that long journeys may be a problem for students who live far away, although more evidence is needed. The conclusion is that the school bus is the most common way to travel. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a second morning bus, which would probably shorten the daily commute. The survey was somewhat limited, so the results should be treated as tentative.
accepted: The aim of this report is to describe how students travel to school. The method was a survey of 100 students carried out by the school council, and every answer was included in the analysis. The main findings show that 52 percent of respondents come by school bus, whereas only 6 percent cycle. The remaining students either walk, 30 percent, or come by car, 12 percent. Furthermore, 35 students said that the bus journey takes more than forty minutes. It appears that long journeys may be a problem for students who live far away, although more evidence is needed. The conclusion is that the school bus is the most common way to travel. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a second morning bus, which would probably shorten the daily commute. The survey was somewhat limited, so the results should be treated as tentative.

This report gives an overview of how students get to school. A survey of 100 students was carried out by the school council. The findings show that more than half of the respondents, 52 percent, use the school bus, while 30 percent walk, 12 percent come by car and only 6 percent cycle. In addition, 35 students said that the journey by bus takes longer than forty minutes. There is some evidence that long journeys may affect students who live far away, but it remains unclear how many are affected. To conclude, the bus is the main way to travel. We recommend that the school consider an extra bus in the morning, which would shorten the daily commute for many families.

The aim of this report is to show how students travel to school. We surveyed 100 students, and every student answered in class, so all the replies could be included. According to the survey, 52 percent travel by school bus, 30 percent walk, 12 percent come by car and 6 percent cycle. Nevertheless, the bus is not always convenient: 35 students said that the journey takes over forty minutes. It seems that this may be a problem for those who live far away, although the survey cannot prove it. Therefore, we recommend a second morning bus. The conclusion is that the school bus is essential, and a second one could improve the daily commute for many students.

feedback.es: El mini informe lleva el objetivo, los resultados con cifras, una afirmación matizada, la conclusión y una recomendación, con tono neutro.

origin.text: Encuesta del consejo escolar a 100 estudiantes sobre cómo llegan al colegio: 52 en autobús escolar, 30 a pie, 12 en coche y 6 en bicicleta. El viaje en autobús dura más de 40 minutos para 35 estudiantes. Escribe unas 140 a 220 palabras: objetivo, método, resultados con cifras, una afirmación matizada, la conclusión y una recomendación, con tono neutro.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador y elige qué debería mejorar el resumen oral.

choices.text: It lists too many figures and lacks a clear key point.
It sounds too informal and includes too many personal opinions.
It should have started with the recommendation instead of the figures.

feedback.es: El borrador enumera cinco cifras seguidas sin decir cuál importa: falta una idea clave que el público pueda recordar.

origin.text: Draft of a one-minute summary: 'Our survey asked 100 students about transport. We found that 52 came by bus, 30 walked, 12 came by car and 6 cycled. Also 35 said that the bus takes more than forty minutes, 22 said that it is sometimes late and 14 said that it is crowded.'

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué repetirá la estudiante la idea clave al final.

choices.text: Because the written report did not include that point.
Because listeners cannot go back and read it again.
Because she has to fill the whole minute with something.

feedback.es: Al no poder releer, el oyente necesita que la idea central se repita al final.

origin.audio: A student is comparing her written report with her oral summary. The report has a method section and a long list of findings. In the talk she will skip the method and mention only two findings, because the listeners cannot read the tables. She will repeat the key point at the end, so nobody forgets it.

prompt.es: Escribe el resumen oral de un minuto con anuncio, punto clave, cautela y recomendación.

answer.text: I will outline the main findings of our survey on digital habits. The key point is that 64 of the 80 students use a phone for more than three hours a day. Only a minority, 20 students, sleep fewer than seven hours. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. To conclude, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.
accepted: I will outline the main findings of our survey on digital habits. The key point is that 64 of the 80 students use a phone for more than three hours a day. Only a minority, 20 students, sleep fewer than seven hours. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. To conclude, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.

I will briefly present our survey on digital habits. The main point is that most students, 64 out of 80, use a phone for more than three hours daily. It seems that heavy users may sleep less, but we cannot be sure. Only 20 students sleep fewer than seven hours. In conclusion, we recommend one hour without phones before bed.

I will give an overview of our digital habits survey. The key finding is that 64 of our 80 students use a phone for over three hours a day. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. In short, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.

feedback.es: El resumen anuncia, da el punto clave con una cifra, añade una cautela y cierra con una recomendación, en frases cortas.

origin.text: Encuesta sobre hábitos digitales (80 estudiantes): 64 usan el móvil más de tres horas al día; solo 20 duermen menos de siete horas; los que más lo usan parecen dormir menos. Escribe el resumen oral de un minuto (50 a 110 palabras): anuncio, punto clave con cifra, cautela y recomendación.
